punchline: The first logged computer bug was a real moth, taped into the Harvard Mark II logbook with a dry note that it was the first actual case.
thirty_sec: In September 1947, operators of the Harvard Mark II hunted for a fault and found a moth trapped in a relay. They taped it into the logbook and wrote 'First actual case of bug being found.' The word 'bug' was already old engineers' slang, so the line was a joke. Grace Hopper's team helped spread the story, and the page now sits with the Smithsonian.
